title: Feasibility and acceptability of oral cholera vaccine mass vaccination campaign in response to an outbreak and floods in Malawi.
ehr_evidence: This study made use of the available health facility data and reports on cholera outbreak and oral cholera vaccine campaign.
summary: Documentation of the feasibility, acceptability, and coverage of a reactive mass oral cholera vaccine campaign in Nsanje district, Malawi, following floods and a cholera outbreak.
key_findings: Round 1 campaign achieved 97.6% coverage (156,592 of 160,482 target population).
Round 2 achieved 85.8% coverage (137,629 recipients), with 67.6% fully immunized (108,247).
Demographics of vaccinated individuals showed 54.4% females and 55.4% children under 15 years.
No severe adverse events following immunization were reported.
The main reason for non-vaccination or incomplete dosing was absence during the campaign period.
The 2014/2015 cholera outbreak across eight districts resulted in 693 cases and 11 deaths (CFR 1.6%).
study_design: descriptive documentation of a mass vaccination campaign
data_source_type: health facility registers and administrative reports
population: over 160,000 people aged one year or more in 19 displacement camps and surrounding communities in Nsanje district, Malawi
limitations: Reliance on health facility data and reports leads to incompleteness and bias.
Information only obtained from individuals who visited health facilities.
Data on non-vaccinated individuals could not be captured.
